claims.text: Depositing a 2–3 nm conformal ceria overlayer will lower the catalyst's low-temperature oxidation light-off temperature.
Depositing a conformal ceria overlayer will improve resistance to poisoning by H2O and NO.
Depositing a conformal ceria overlayer will improve long-term catalyst durability.
Adding the ceria overlayer will not increase platinum-group-metal content.
The starting catalyst is a near-equiatomic multi-principal-element alloy containing elements such as Cu, Ni, Pd, and Pt.
ALD of ceria onto the alloy surface creates an active metal/oxide interface.
The ceria-containing interface provides oxygen-storage capability.
The ceria-containing interface generates oxygen vacancies.
Oxygen storage and release by ceria supplies reactive oxygen species that facilitate CO oxidation at lower temperatures.
Oxygen storage and release by ceria supplies reactive oxygen species that facilitate hydrocarbon oxidation at lower temperatures.
Conformal ceria coverage acts as a physical barrier that reduces H2O adsorption on critical catalytic sites.
Conformal ceria coverage acts as a physical barrier that reduces NO adsorption on critical catalytic sites.
The thermal stability of ceria protects the alloy catalyst against sintering during long-term harsh exhaust exposure.
Protection against sintering reduces long-term catalytic deactivation.
Relative to the unmodified catalyst, the ceria-modified catalyst will maintain more activity after accelerated aging.
The unmodified near-equiatomic alloy degrades under combined low-temperature, poisoning, and extended-use conditions.
The predicted benefits apply to CO and hydrocarbon oxidation below 150 °C in exhaust containing H2O and NO.
Ceria overlayers are known to enhance oxidation catalysis and durability in related catalyst systems.
Integration of ceria overlayers with nearly equiatomic multi-principal-element alloys is less explored.
